name: contract_ramp_503
description: Contract test for backpressure shedding: an 80-agent fleet, fully unpaced (concurrent_agents 0, requests_per_second 0), replaying a large syscollector delta (150 docs x 16 KiB, ~2.4 MiB/session) back-to-back for a FIXED DURATION rather than a fixed session count -- a fast manager just admits more sessions in the same window before any one of them drains, so the pressure is self-scaling and the shed still triggers regardless of hardware. The gate this exercises is the pipeline's own admission queue (`inventory_sync_server_sync_queue_bytes`, default 64 MiB, a global byte counter checked at enqueue before a session reaches its shard) -- confirmed via GET /metrics (`sync.pipeline.shed.total` > 0 during the run), not the indexer-availability path session_storm's sustained flood happens to trip instead, nor the transport's far larger `max_inflight_bytes` (256 MiB). 503 responses here are expected backpressure behavior, not a failure. 503s are the MEASUREMENT here, so the agent-like retry is disabled (retry.enabled=false).
